one_liner: libjpeg-turbo fork that trades much slower JPEG encoding for smaller files; it is not faster than libjpeg-turbo at anything.
what_it_does: A patched libjpeg-turbo that writes smaller standard JPEGs: by default jpeg_set_defaults() picks the JCP_MAX_COMPRESSION profile (progressive with scan search, optimized Huffman tables, AC+DC trellis quantization, overshoot deringing, quant table set 3). It keeps the libjpeg API and ABI, so programs that link against libjpeg get the new defaults without code changes. Extra settings go through an accessor framework (jpeg_c_set_bool_param, jpeg_c_set_int_param, jpeg_c_set_float_param), and the JCP_FASTEST profile (cjpeg -revert) restores plain libjpeg-turbo behavior. jpegtran losslessly re-optimizes existing JPEGs with the same scan search; the decoder is libjpeg-turbo's, unchanged.
how_it_is_fast: It is not; the work goes into file size. For 3-component YCbCr, jpeg_search_progression() sets up 64 candidate scans (23 for grayscale). Each candidate gets a Huffman-statistics pass and an output pass into an in-memory buffer, and select_scans() then keeps the smallest combination (jpgcrush-style). That makes at least 128 entropy passes before trellis. Trellis quantization (quantize_trellis in jcdctmgr.c) is a scalar float rate-distortion search per 8x8 block, with lambda = 2^14.75 / ((2^16.5 + n) * q^2) by default. It runs 2 passes per component per trellis loop over the saved unquantized coefficients of the whole image. The speed it does have is libjpeg-turbo's: SIMD color conversion, downsampling, forward DCT and baseline Huffman.
when_to_use: Offline or build-time compression of web images (static-site pipelines, CDN pre-processing, image optimizers), where encoding runs once and the smaller file is downloaded many times.
Lossless recompression of existing JPEGs with jpegtran (progressive plus scan search), when you cannot re-encode from pixels.
Programs already on the libjpeg API that want smaller output without code changes: relink and jpeg_set_defaults() turns on the max-compression profile.
As the reference encoder when you evaluate size-for-quality JPEG encoders such as mozjpeg-rs, zenjpeg or jpegli, all of which benchmark against it.
when_not_to_use: Real-time or per-request encoding (thumbnail proxies, camera or video frames, screenshots). Its own README-mozilla.txt says it is considerably slower than libjpeg-turbo, and even than libjpeg, at default settings. In mozjpeg-rs's README, C mozjpeg needs 210 ms with trellis against 9 ms for Huffman-optimized baseline on a 2048x2048 image (about 23x, derived from page data; hardware not stated).

As a speed upgrade for decoding: decoding is libjpeg-turbo's code. Its default progressive output also decodes slower than baseline in libjpeg-turbo: zenjpeg's README (Ryzen 9 7950X) lists 34 MiB/s for progressive against 78.1 MiB/s for baseline 4:2:0, possibly on different files.

Memory-constrained encoding of large images: trellis keeps quantized and unquantized whole-image coefficient arrays (whole_image and whole_image_uq in jccoefct.c), and scan optimization buffers every candidate scan in memory.

Processes or distro packages that also need stock libjpeg-turbo: both ship libjpeg/libturbojpeg with the same names and symbols. Issue #382, open since 2020, asks for a separately named libmozjpeg, and PR #383 has been open since then.

Projects that track upstream security fixes through tagged releases: the latest tag is v4.1.1, built on libjpeg-turbo 2.1.3. The libjpeg-turbo 3.0.x merge on master (January 2025, CMake VERSION 5.0.0) is untagged.

integration.form: static lib and shared lib (libjpeg API library plus TurboJPEG library), CMake build; cjpeg, djpeg and jpegtran tools
integration.dependencies: none for the library; NASM 2.13+ or Yasm 1.2.0+ for x86 SIMD; cjpeg PNG input needs libpng 1.6 and zlib (PNG_SUPPORTED defaults to TRUE; turn it off if libpng is absent)
integration.min_toolchain: C89-era C compiler (GCC 4.1+ or Clang recommended, Visual C++ 2005+), CMake 2.8.12+
integration.platforms: Same as libjpeg-turbo: x86, x86-64, Arm/aarch64 (Neon), PowerPC (AltiVec), MIPS (MMI) SIMD, plus a C fallback anywhere; Linux, macOS, Windows
integration.thread_safety: Same as libjpeg: one jpeg_compress_struct per thread. The library is not thread-safe on a shared object (libjpeg.txt), and the encoder itself is single-threaded.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: libjpeg API and ABI drop-in with smaller, slower output under default settings. Through the TurboJPEG API it is not a size upgrade, because setCompDefaults() in turbojpeg.c forces JCP_FASTEST and so behaves like plain libjpeg-turbo.

gotchas: Default output can be corrupted by a SIMD FDCT overflow, open as of 2026-10-05. Overshoot deringing (on by default) can push level-shifted samples to +/-158. The 16-bit wrapping adds in the SIMD islow forward DCT (SSE2, AVX2, MMX, Neon, MMI, AltiVec) then overflow (8 x 5056 = 40448), which flips the sign of DC/low-AC coefficients and leaves inverted-brightness 8x8 blocks (issue #444). PR #453 switches these to saturating adds and reports 2 of 639 test encodes changed. The C DCT path is not affected; -noovershoot avoids the bug.

TurboJPEG API callers (tjCompress2/tj3Compress8, and tjbench) get libjpeg-turbo behavior, because turbojpeg.c sets JCP_FASTEST before jpeg_set_defaults(). To get mozjpeg's gains, use the libjpeg API or set the extension parameters yourself.

jpeg_set_defaults() resets every mozjpeg parameter from JINT_COMPRESS_PROFILE. Set the profile first, then quality and the extensions. mozjpeg-rs's README warns that the Rust mozjpeg crate's setters silently undo earlier settings for the same reason.

Output size is not monotonic across releases: issue #433 (open) shows jpegtran in 4.1.1 producing larger files than 3.1 on some inputs (402,438 vs 400,769 bytes on lab.jpg). PNG input in cjpeg is broken in the current CMake build (issue #450, fix PR #455 unmerged).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick C mozjpeg over libjpeg-turbo only when file size matters more than encode time; over mozjpeg-rs when you need the C libjpeg ABI, jpegtran's lossless recompression or the fastest Huffman-only path (mozjpeg-rs's README has C at 9 ms vs Rust 42 ms for baseline); prefer mozjpeg-rs for memory-safe Rust or slightly faster trellis (197 vs 210 ms in its README), and look at jpegli or zenjpeg when you want better quality per byte at much lower encode cost.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing here measures a speed win. The project itself says it compresses considerably slower than libjpeg-turbo with default settings. Third-party figures agree but lack full methodology: the 2014-era sergejmueller gist has jpegtran -progressive about 2.3x slower; oximg issue #61 (Zen 4, 512 px, q80) has trellis at 10316 us per image. mozjpeg-rs's README (2048x2048, 30 iterations, AVX2, CPU not stated) shows C mozjpeg at 210 ms with trellis against 9 ms Huffman-optimized baseline. Search-result snippets, apparently from libjpeg-turbo.org/About/Mozjpeg (page blocked, not opened, source not certain), put jpgcrush plus trellis at about 4-7x the encoding time of plain progressive for 4-15% better compression.
status_note: Stale: the last commit is 2025-06-23 and the last tag is v4.1.1 (libjpeg-turbo 2.1.3), and six PRs sit unreviewed or in review, including the FDCT overflow fix. Licensed IJG, BSD-3-Clause and zlib, and safe to use as an offline size optimizer, but not a performance pick.
